title: Lapse of Spendable Points on a Wanderlane Traveller Club Card
content:
**Clause 1. The expiry term and the order of lapse.** Spendable points on a Wanderlane Traveller Club card lapse at the end of the expiry term of the tier held when they were earned, counted from the date they posted, and lapse row by row so that the oldest points always leave first. The term read is the term of the tier the member held when those points were earned, and each credit on the card carries its own expiry date counted from its own posting date.

**Clause 2. Where activity extends the clock.** On a tier whose expiry extends with activity, any qualifying activity resets the clock on the whole balance rather than on the individual accrual. On a tier whose expiry does not extend with activity, each credit runs out its own term from its own posting date.

**Clause 3. Lapse of the membership itself.** A membership that lapses for inactivity sweeps its whole spendable balance in one movement, and those points are reinstated only if the membership itself is reinstated first.

**Clause 4. Qualifying points.** Qualifying points never lapse: they are cleared down when the period ends and are never swept for age.

## The two orders of lapse compared

| What lapses | How it leaves the card |
| --- | --- |
| Points reaching the end of their expiry term | Row by row, the oldest points always leaving first |
| The whole balance on a membership that falls dormant for inactivity | In one movement, the whole spendable balance at once |

## A hypothetical card, read through

A card holds three credits, posted in March, in July and in November of one year, on a tier whose expiry does not extend with activity. Each credit runs out the expiry term of the tier held when it was earned, counted from its own posting date, so the March credit reaches the end of its term first and leaves first, then the July credit, then the November credit. Had the same card been held at a tier whose expiry extends with activity, a single piece of qualifying activity would have reset the clock on the whole balance, all three credits together, rather than on the credit that produced it.
